nodes.name: Co-precipitation of Co-ZIF on CC
nodes.procedure: cobalt nitrate and dimethylimidazole as raw materials to uniformly grow triangular-structured cobalt-based imidazolium zeolite skeleton compounds (Co-ZIF) on carbon cloth (CC) using a simple co-precipitation method.
nodes.source_text: Herein, we used cobalt nitrate and dimethylimidazole as raw materials to uniformly grow triangular-structured cobalt-based imidazolium zeolite skeleton compounds (Co-ZIF) on carbon cloth (CC) using a simple co-precipitation method.

nodes.name: Molybdate corrosion and annealing
nodes.procedure: Co-ZIF material with a triangular structure was uniformly grown on CC by the coprecipitation method. Subsequently, it was immersed in sodium molybdate solution and annealed in air to obtain Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC (Figure 1a; Figure S1, Supporting Information). Immersion in a solution containing MoO4^2- broke the Co-Hmim bond causing it to replace some of the Hmim, resulting in the color of Co-ZIF changing from purple to brown and the smooth surface becoming wrinkled. The soaking time to generate Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC is investigated. The optimal soaking time is 30 min.

nodes.method: directed corrosion strategy and heat treatment
nodes.source_text: Co-ZIF material with a triangular structure was uniformly grown on CC by the coprecipitation method. Subsequently, it was immersed in sodium molybdate solution and annealed in air to obtain Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC... The optimal soaking time is 30 min.

nodes.name: Direct air annealing of Co-ZIF
nodes.procedure: The direct air annealing of Co-ZIF shows that the front surface of the triangle is smooth... Annealing Hmim ligands in the air will still form NOC sheets. Based on this, Co-ZIF is directly calcined to form a composite CC material with Co3O4 anchored on NOC (Co3O4@NOC/CC).
nodes.source_text: The direct air annealing of Co-ZIF shows that the front surface of the triangle is smooth... Based on this, Co-ZIF is directly calcined to form a composite CC material with Co3O4 anchored on NOC (Co3O4@NOC/CC).

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M Na₂SO₄ solution
nodes.source_text: The OER catalytic performance of the catalysts was characterized in a three-electrode system and 1MNa₂SO₄ solution... Mo - Co₃O₄@NOC / CC exhibits excellent OER catalytic performance. It can reach 10mAcm⁻² at an ultra-low overpotential of 289 mV... overpotential is only 380 mV at 50mAcm⁻²... Tafel slopes ... 49mVdec⁻¹... Cdl value (56mFcm⁻²)

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in flow cell with neutral medium
nodes.source_text: In a neutral medium, a current density of 500mA cm⁻² at room temperature requires a voltage of 1.71V. It only needs a voltage of 1.82V to reach the industrial current density (1.0Acm⁻²)... the H₂ generation rate is 466.1 mL cm⁻² h⁻¹, and the energy consumption is only 4.36KWhNm⁻³H₂

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in real seawater flow cell
nodes.source_text: In the real seawater flow cell... a voltage of 1.79V is required to achieve a current density of 500mA cm⁻² at room temperature in real seawater. A voltage of 1.94V is required to achieve an industrial current density of 1.0Acm⁻²... the H₂ generation rate in real seawater is 418.6 mLcm⁻²h⁻¹, and the energy consumption is only 4.64 KWh Nm⁻³H₂... continuous electrolysis at 1Acm⁻² for 300h exhibits almost no decay... Faraday efficiency of producing O₂ and H₂ is close to 100%

nodes.description: OER stability test after 3000 CV cycles in 1 M Na₂SO₄
nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 3g, the polarization curves of the catalysts hardly changed after 3000 CV cycling, indicating that the catalyst has good stability under different currents.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC surface appears wrinkled with many pores generated, similar to hollow structure becoming rough.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Co3O4@ NOC/CC, the surface of Mo-Co3O4@ NOC/CC appears wrinkled (Figure 1b), and there are many pores generated, which is similar to the hollow structure becoming rough (Figure S6, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC composed of nanoparticles (~7 nm diameter) and thin NOC sheets; Co3O4@NOC/CC nanoparticles ~12 nm diameter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images that the diameter distribution of Co3O4 nanoparticles in Co3O4@ NOC/CC is mainly ≈12 nm... The diameter of nanoparticles in Mo-Co3O4@ NOC/CC is mainly ≈7 nm (Figure 1c inset).

nodes.characterization_summary: Both catalysts show Co3O4 (311) plane at 0.24 nm lattice spacing; Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC exhibits lattice distortion, Vo, and rich-micropores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images that the lattice spacing of Co3O4@ NOC/CC and Mo-Co3O4@ NOC/CC sample is 0.24 nm, which corresponds to the (311) plane of Co3O4... After MoO42- corrosion, the lattice of Co3O4 shows defects such as lattice distortion, Vo, and rich-micropores (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Single Mo atoms (0.26 nm diameter) highly dispersed on Co3O4 lattice, preferentially at defect edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Figure 1g, the aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM, single Mo atomic bright spots are observed to be highly dispersed on the lattice of Co3O4... the diameter of a single Mo atom is c.a. 0.26 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co, Mo, N, and O uniformly distributed on NOC nanosheets of Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) elemental mapping images show that Co, Mo, N, and O are uniformly distributed on the NOC nanosheets (Figure 1i).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo content in Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC catalyst is 2.12 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) analysis, the Mo content in the catalyst is 2.12 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC shows weaker Co3O4 characteristic peaks than Co3O4@NOC/CC, indicating decreased crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Co3O4@NOC / CC, the characteristic peak of Co3O4 in Mo- Co3O4@NOC / CC is weaker (Figure S11, Supporting Information), indicating that the crystallinity of the material decreases...

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge XANES position between MoN and MoO3 indicates oxidation state between references; FT-EXAFS shows Mo-O peak at 1.4 Å (blue-shifted vs MoO3) with coordination number ~6 confirming atomic MoO6 dispersion at Co3O4 interface; no Mo-Mo peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, the average oxidation state of Mo species is proved by the K-edge XANES of Mo in various samples. Apparently, the position of the Mo- Co3O4@NOC / CC is located between MoN and MoO3... From Figure 2b, the Mo- Co3O4@NOC / CC exhibits an obvious FT peak at 1.4Å... the O coordination number in the sample is close to 6... In addition, Mo-Mo peaks are not observed in the Mo- Co3O4@NOC / CC compared to Mo foils, Mo2C, and MoN

nodes.characterization_summary: Co3O4@NOC/CC characteristic peaks at 483.1, 525.1, 691.5 cm⁻¹; Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC peaks blue-shifted and weakened.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Figure 2c, the Raman characteristic peaks of Co3O4@NOC / CC distinctly appear at the displacement of 483.1, 525.1, and 691.5 cm⁻¹... Compared with Co3O4@NOC / CC, the three characteristic peaks of Mo- Co3O4@NOC / CC are blue shifted, and the peak intensity is also weakened...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p in Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC: Co3+ at 781.3/796.3 eV, Co2+ peaks red-shifted vs Co3O4@NOC/CC (779.8/794.9 eV Co3+); greater Co3+ shift indicates Mo anchoring at Co3+ sites; Mo 3d shows Mo6+ > Mo4+ confirming MoO6; O 1s M-O bond shifts to lower binding energy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Figure 2d, the Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2 orbitals with binding energies corresponding to Co3+ at 779.8 and 794.9 eV in Co3O4@NOC/C samples... Compared with Co3O4@NOC/C, both Co3+ and Co2+ of Mo- Co3O4@NOC/CC have a red shift, which indicates that Mo atomic changes the central electronic structure of Co. Significantly, the binding energy difference of Co3+ red shift is higher than that of Co2+... In the Mo 3d spectra (Figure S14, Supporting Information), Mo6+ and Mo4+ are presented... Mo6+ possesses a higher content compared to Mo4+... In the O 2p spectrum of XPS (Figure 2e), the M-O bond in Mo- Co3O4@NOC / CC shifts to lower binding energy

nodes.characterization_summary: Both catalysts show g=2.004 indicating abundant Vo; Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC has more Vo than Co3O4@NOC/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2h, the electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectral g-value of the Co3O4@NOC / CC and Mo Co3O4@NOC / CC samples is ≈2.004 indicating that the annealing process... produced abundant Vo.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC Cdl = 56 mF cm⁻² > other catalysts, indicating largest electrochemically active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3d, Mo- Co3O4@NOC / CC possesses the largest Cdl value (56 mFcm⁻²), which indicates that the catalyst exhibits a larger specific surface area and more active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC specific surface area significantly increased compared to Co3O4@NOC/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the specific surface area is significantly increased (Figure S7, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns verify decreased crystallinity of Mo-Co3O4@NOC/CC compared to Co3O4@NOC/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns of various samples verify this hypothesis (Figure S10, Supporting Information).
